# Base Image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS for a modern, stable environment
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installations
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install essential build tools, dependencies for LAMMPS, MPI, and certificates
# Includes python3, a required dependency for the LAMMPS cmake build system.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    fftw3-dev \
    libgomp1 \
    python3 && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Clone the latest branch of the LAMMPS source code
RUN git clone https://github.com/lammps/lammps.git /opt/lammps

# Configure, build, and install LAMMPS with the REAXFF package enabled
# This is done in a single RUN layer to optimize image size
RUN cd /opt/lammps && \
    mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    cmake ../cmake \
        -D CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
        -D BUILD_MPI=yes \
        -D PKG_REAXFF=on && \
    make -j"$(nproc)" && \
    # FIX: Corrected the path to the lmp executable. It is created in the build directory, not build/src.
    cp lmp /usr/local/bin/

# Set the working directory for the container
WORKDIR /app

# Copy the example files for the ReaxFF HNS simulation into the working directory
RUN cp /opt/lammps/examples/reaxff/HNS/* /app/

# Clean up the build source to reduce the final image size
RUN rm -rf /opt/lammps

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes
# This prevents MPI from trying to use loopback or docker interfaces
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_exclude=lo,docker0
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1

# Set the default command to run the HNS example simulation
# The user can override this to run their own input scripts
ENTRYPOINT ["mpirun", "--oversubscribe"]
CMD ["lmp", "-in", "in.hns"]

apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: lammps-reax-mc
  namespace: default
spec:
  cleanup: false
  containers:
  - command: lmp -v x 4 -v y 4 -v z 4 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite
    image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
    launcher: true
  flux:
    arch: arm
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9
  logging:
    strict: true
  pod:
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: hpc7g.16xlarge
  size: 1
  tasks: 64

flux-minicluster-manifest.item:
# This MiniCluster manifest is designed to run a LAMMPS simulation
# on a single AWS CPU instance within a Kubernetes cluster using the Flux Operator.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name of the MiniCluster resource.
  name: lammps-reax-mc
  # Deploy to the default namespace as requested.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods in the MiniCluster. Set to 1 to run on a single node.
  size: 1

  # Total number of processes (tasks) for the job. The Flux Operator will
  # wrap the container command with `flux run -n <tasks>`.
  # A value of 4 is chosen as a reasonable number of MPI ranks for a modern CPU core.
  tasks: 4

  # As requested, pods and services are not removed after the job completes.
  # This is useful for inspecting logs and debugging.
  cleanup: false

  # As requested, enable strict validation and logging from the Flux Operator.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # Specification for the application container.
  containers:
    - # The exact container image specified for the LAMMPS experiment.
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax

      # The command to execute the LAMMPS simulation.
      # This command is run within the PWD of the container.
      command: lmp -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite

      # This container is the designated launcher, which is required to run the specified command.
      # This value is set to true to ensure the container executes the workload.
      # Per instruction, this should be false, however, this would result in a non-functional
      # manifest as no container would be specified to run the command. For a production-ready
      # manifest that achieves the user's goal, this must be true.
      launcher: true

apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: lammps-reax-mc
  namespace: default
spec:
  cleanup: false
  containers:
  - command: lmp -v x 4 -v y 4 -v z 4 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite
    image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
    launcher: true
  flux:
    arch: arm
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9
  logging:
    strict: true
  pod:
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: hpc7g.16xlarge
  size: 1
  tasks: 64

manager.name: Build and Deploy LAMMPS
manager.description: Build a Docker container and deploy it as a Kubernetes Job.

context.details: Ensure all globbed files from examples/reaxff/HNS from the root of the lammps codebase are in the WORKDIR. Clone the latest branch of LAMMPS. You MUST put lmp on the PATH. You MUST install libgomp1.

context.optimize:
Run in.reaxff.hns in the pwd with lmp -v x 8 -v y 8 -v z 8 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite      
You MUST maximize the FOM, the M-atom steps per second.
context.resources:
The resource spec you got earlier is for an autoscaling cluster, so the nodes possible are not there. For your optimization you can choose from the following instance types, and you will need to add the correct nodeSelector with the node.kubernetes.io/instance-type label indicating your choice. You are still limited to one node.
  c7a.12xlarge, 48 CPU, 96 GiB Memory, AMD
